subject: Architecture
title: Biophilic Design: Nature Inside Architecture
description: A quick, practical guide to Biophilic Design: Nature Inside Architecture.

hook.text: Humans spend 90% of their time indoors, yet our brains are wired to crave nature.

buildup.text: Biophilic design brings nature into buildings — living walls, water features, natural light, and wood.

discovery.text: Studies show biophilic offices increase productivity by 15% and reduce sick days by 10%.

twist.text: Amazon's Spheres in Seattle house 40,000 plants inside glass domes — an office that's also a rainforest.

climax.text: Hospitals using biophilic design report patients healing faster and needing less pain medication.

punchline.text: Plants in the office aren't decoration. They're medicine.

quiz.question: What measurable effect does biophilic design have on office workers?
options: It doubles the number of job applicants

details.summary: Biophilic design integrates natural elements — plants, water, daylight, natural materials, and views of nature — into buildings to improve occupant health, productivity, and wellbeing.
details.whyItMatters: Humans evolved in nature and our brains still respond to it. Biophilic design applies that science to architecture, creating buildings that actively support human health rather than merely housing human activity.
takeaways: Biophilic design integrates nature into built environments
Research shows it reduces stress and boosts productivity
It applies evolutionary science to architectural practice

faq.question: What are examples of biophilic design in buildings?
faq.answer: Amazon's Spheres in Seattle (indoor rainforest workspace), Bosco Verticale in Milan (apartments with balcony forests), Singapore's Jewel Changi Airport (indoor waterfall and gardens). Even simpler interventions like daylight, timber surfaces, and green walls qualify.

faq.question: Does biophilic design actually improve health?
faq.answer: Yes. Studies show 15% higher productivity in offices with natural elements, faster hospital recovery rates with nature views, and measurably lower cortisol levels in biophilic environments. The evidence is strong enough that many building certifications now require biophilic elements.
